 3. Based on supportive evidence, what are the important nutri-
tion factors to keep in mind when treating patients of various 
age groups with asthma?
Nutritional implications for AD are uniquely associated 
with altered brain function with regard to general cognition
as well as feeding behavior.
• Amnesia: In the early stages of the disease, aﬀ ected
persons may ﬁ nd it challenging to shop for groceries,
prepare foods, and remember whether or not they have
eaten. As AD progresses, they may no longer remember 
what to do with food and utensils placed in front of them 
and require increasing assistance and encouragement 
from caregivers in order to consume suﬃ  cient nutrients.
• Apraxia: Chewing diﬃ  culty and dysphagia may also 
occur in the late stages of the disease. Confusion and
